severities.name: blocker
severities.definition: Data loss or corruption, a security failure (authorisation, tenant isolation, secrets, injection, untrusted instructions obeyed), a broken build or release, or an access-rule violation (the spec's Access section or the org's input standards make the product unusable for a class of user).
severities.requiredAction: Fix before merge, or a waiver approved by Justin through Atlas with an expiry. The issue cannot move to Done while an unwaived S0 is open.
examples: Migration drops a column without backfill
Payment mutation replayed without an idempotency key

severities.name: major
severities.definition: A user-visible bug on a supported path, a declared state, event or action that is missing, a serious accessibility failure (no name, no keyboard path, no visible focus, hover- or drag-only), a finding with no evidence, or a spec or ADR that cannot be verified.
severities.requiredAction: Fix before merge when more than three S1 are open; otherwise fix or record a waiver approved by Sentinel (security S1 need Justin) with an expiry and a Linear issue. The review pass does not move an issue to Done with an unwaived S1.

severities.name: minor
severities.definition: A defect with a workaround or limited exposure: misalignment of 4 px or more, a theme leak, N+1 on a small list, a test that asserts nothing, a missing changelog fragment, a denied write attempt by a reviewer.
severities.requiredAction: Fix in this PR when cheap, otherwise a follow-up issue linked from the finding. Never blocks; trended weekly by the calibration auditor.

severities.name: nit
severities.definition: Polish: wording, intentional truncation with a tooltip, repeated cheap work, third-party code findings (pointer to PAP-216), missing Spanish strings.
severities.requiredAction: Author's discretion. Batched into polish passes.

severities.name: question
severities.definition: A possible defect the reviewer could not confirm (confidence under 0.5), a request for context, or a waived finding shown for the record.
severities.requiredAction: Author answers in the thread; the reviewer may upgrade to a defect with evidence on the next round.
examples: Contrast computed at 3.2:1, borderline for large text
Is this list bounded by construction?

severities.name: praise
severities.definition: Something worth repeating: a test that would catch a real regression, a clean boundary, a good edge case.
severities.requiredAction: None. Counted so reviewers are calibrated on what good looks like, not only what is wrong.
examples: Empty state with a clear next action

gateRule.statement: Any S0 blocks. More than 3 S1 block. S2 and S3 never block. A defect finding with confidence under 0.5 posts as a question. Waived findings (unexpired waiver) count as questions.

caps.note: Point at the generator; the fix lands in the source.
Pointer to PAP-216 (dependency policy); vulnerabilities go through PAP-80 instead.

approvals.S2 and S3: any reviewer or the author with a linked issue

waiver.rule: A severity override is recorded as a waiver on the finding, never as a silent edit of the severity. Expired waivers stop applying and fail release certification (PAP-88).
